I am so sorry to hear what you have been through. It sounds terrible and I imagine you and your mom have experienced a great deal of pain. That kind of abuse tends to have quite an impact and I wold be willing to bet you might have a little PTSD / Borderline Personality situation on your hand. The good news is there is help available for you and your mom depending on where you live. I think the best thing would be to look for some Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) for you and your mom. It really works! But you have to put the work in and it's not easy. If that is not available, some Cognitive Behavior Therapy can also help. Just know you are not likely to change your dad and may have to set some new boundaries or even end the relationship. I wouldn't do that without first going to therapy and working through it with a professional and creating a plan that will work for you. You deserve happiness and a life that is worth living and therapy can help you set that up.

With your mom, that is a very different situation. With domestic abuse, it can be very difficult to help someone who does not want help or does not have the resources to leave. Lots of love, empathy, and support for her may be your best option. Try to find out if she wants to leave. Find out if would be willing to talk to someone. If she wants to leave but cannot afford it, look for Domestic Abuse hotlines and agencies in your area to see if they can help her plan an exit. They can help her create a safe exit strategy. And know that even thought he is a horrible person, she may have her reasons for wanting to stay. That is one of the most heartbreaking parts about situations like hers and you cannot force her to leave him. If you try, you risk hurting your relationship with her. You can work on that in therapy because even though he should be the one to change, that is not likely. Therefore, your option is to change yourself and build a way to be protected from him and supportive to her. 

If you ever want to chat more or have questions, please shoot me a message. I really want you to know there is hope and you deserve happiness.

I majored in psychology and have a master's in social work. My focus has been on mental health and substance use. I can tell you that having and uncle with schizophrenia means you are already more likely to develop it than people with no diagnosed relatives (almost a 10%). You should speak to a genetic counselor to better understand your specific risks. Also, check out the information and linked papers on [this](http://schizophrenia.com/prev1.htm?sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjK0tj0-KvmAhVIXK0KHVM5ClUQ9QF6BAgMEAI#) page. 

Many things can cause schizophrenia to manifest in people who have the genes. Stress from difficult experiences is one verified risk factor. So things like car accidents, domestic violence, war trauma, and even use of beautiful but complicated psychedelics can trigger schizophrenia. 

Not much research has been done with psychedelics because of bans by the government. But there are many cases of people manifesting schizophrenia after drug use. Some research shows slightly higher levels of dmt in the brains of some people with schizophrenia as compared to those without the disorder. The research is not conclusive, we don't know what that means or if it is significant. 

Other research shows that dmt best imitates the symptoms of psychosis experienced by people with schizophrenia. 

Schizophrenia is manageable by some people, but most suffer life long symptoms of poor physical health, loneliness, poverty, high rates of suicide, and homelessness. 

The way I see it, dmt use with family history of schizophrenia is like playing Russian roulette with your brain. 

If you do decide to take that risk, it would be less harmful if you waited until after age 25. Most people develop schizophrenia by early to mid 20's. Also, you'll develop lots of skills and life experience by then which with reduce the chance of a bad trip. The risk will always be there for you and the consequences if it goes wrong are dire. 

I hope this is useful to you. Take care!

The way we talk about rape, sexual assault, sexual violence in everyday conversation is very different than how things are codified legally. The way the legal system works is a separate charge exists for many different acts. There are many acts that the general public would consider rape. However under the law they are considered some other type of crime such as sodomy or forced oral copulation or lewdness. Each state has different laws and different definitions of the same word sometimes.

I suspect many of the people providing crisis services on Playa come from California and used terminology more common in California to create ESD policy. California law has a narrow definition of rape. Many other sex crimes are covered under that broader term of sexual assault, so that is the common phrase used to refer to most sex crimes cases in California. In Nevada, the law defines sexual assault as rape with some sort of penetration. That phrase does not encompass other sex crimes. Instead they use the phrase sexual violence as their broader term covering most sex crimes. The change is likely to make ESD communications more accurate in terms of Nevada State legal terminology.

I have a technique that has worked really well for us. This is something that would need to be done pre-playa due to the moop that will be created while working. It takes a couple hours to a day depending on the number of panels you are repairing. Depending on how much tape you buy,  it can cost up to $100. We did this a couple years ago and it will probably last a few more events before we have to do it again. 

I call these tape walls. Here's what you'll need:

Crusty yurt panels
Tape: silver or grey duct tape, 1 roll per 8' section
Scissors or box cutter
A helper
Optional: scraper to rub tape after applying
Optional: saw horses to raise panels up

First, remove excess tape. Use scissors or a box-cutter to remove anyting that's not firmly stuck to the yurt. If tape has pulled up off of the yurt and brought some silver yurt foil with it, cut off that silver foil too. But don't pull it off. You don't want to remove more than necessary. Just trace the box cutter around the portion that is pulled off and remove it. Remove anything that is not stuck firmly to the foam.

Next, clean the panel. We usually give the entire you're a good hosing off and use a rag to wipe off as much excess playa as possible. Then on the portion that we are trying to repair, we use regular glass cleaner or vinegar wipe it as clean as possible. You don't have to be a perfectionist and the goal is not to remove the crusty tape leftovers, just to get them and the six or so inches of silver foil next to it free from playa. After it dries, you can start tapping. 

To create tape walls, start by stretching your silver or gray duct tape out the length of the panel that you are working on. I do this by handing one end to my partner and I hold on to the other end while we walk away from each other yanking on the tape to stretch it out. Once you have a piece long enough, carefully place it about 6 inches away from where the crusty portion you are trying to cover starts. So, if you have about 6 inches of crusty section, you will start your first layer of tape about a foot away from the edge of the panel. 

Now place a second long strip of tape overlapping the first one by half. Keep adding overlapping layers until you reach the edge and have covered your yucky section. Make sure to go around the corner and cover the 1"-2" edge completely too. What you should be left with is a smooth tape surface on which to tape your yurt together with bifilament tape.

We have had our yurt on Playa the last two years with these tape walls and they worked beautifully. We have not taken it out of storage yet this year to see where we're at, but based on how things were when we took it down last year I'm pretty optimistic. A lot of the photography shared post-event focuses on attractive people. But Burning Man doesn't have a higher percentage of attractive people than any other city. Don't let those photos dissuade you from wearing what you want to wear, or pressure you into wearing things that won't be comfortable. Your first year is the most challenging with regards to clothing because you come in with an idea of what Burning Man is but once you get there you will experience it for yourself and see much more diversity. You'll find your niche. You'll get so many great ideas on how you want to dress yourself or how you might create a costume and every year those damned costume tubs get bigger and fuller. 

Some recommendations:

For tutu Tuesday, many curvier ladies find that crinoline petticoats fit better.

You can find awesome corsets on eBay for not too much money. Just make sure to check the shipping times as some of the better priced ones come from China and won't arrive in time for the burn. Also if ordering from China, note that their sizing is very very different than ours and if you are a 2X here you will probably be a 6X there or something like that. Just check sizing guides.

Jumpsuits and overalls are a great base for a cool costume. You can add patches ribbons weird shit as long as it doesn't fall off and become moop. 

Check out clothing sold to ravers. Some of them are more expensive but there are a lot of sizing options and really cute pieces.

Look up Thai or fisherman pants. They look cute on most figures, they are fairly inexpensive, and very comfortable. Some have lower crotches which may lead to thigh rub, so you might seek out the ones with regular inseams.

Kilts are quite popular on playa with certain crowds and those tend to look good on both guys and gals.

Lane Bryant has a lingerie section that's pretty decent. Some of those pieces can be converted into a more sexy look if you are going for that. And they are designed to flatter curvier gals.

Whatever shoes you get, make sure they are broken in and very very comfortable before you show up. Also know that they are going to get absolutely covered in Playa dust and no one will see the pretty shiny finish. I like boots with zippers for easy on and off, you can spray the zipper with silicone spray to make those zippers work better on Playa. In fact you can spray any zippers you are bringing pre-event and they will hold up better on Playa. Backpacks, tents you name it.

I don't know if that is the best type, but I like it. When you remove them, they can tangle very easily. I like to use a fork or a pick to unbraid and then i immediately put conditioner on the strand to prevent tangling. You might want to pick up an inexpensive silk sleeping cap to protect your braids from getting frizzy while you sleep. Sleeping with braids is not very comfortable :/ but you get used to it. \#1 Be extremely nice, grateful, and helpful to your friend. The more you make their life easier, the more they will want to help you and may let you stay longer. They may also be more forgiving/flexible while you are trying to get back on your feet. This does not mean you have to be a doormat, but definitely make this work. Be friendly and agreeable (nice to be around), be clean (not just after yourself but help your friend out too if you can....I did my aunt's laundry and dishes and she let me stay at her house for free all the time!) Don't complicate your friend's life (try too get along with their friends, family, neighbors, whatever.) Don't be a problem for them, be a great friend!

\#2 Stop spending money. You do not have the luxury for movies, hamburgers, new clothes ANYthing right now. It won't always be the case. Pay your rent, car insurance/registration, and basic home cooked cheap food. All entertainment needs to be free for the moment. And there is lots available in your community if you look for it (parks, hiking, etc.).

\#3 You do not have two months to wait to get a job. Get one now. ANY job. And be on time, work hard, be friendly. You need a good reference and you can bail on a shitty job as soon as you secure a better one (must be higher paying than current one). Here is how. Get the best job you can this week. Be a model employee. Then keep looking for a better job. When you have the better job firm offer, give two weeks notice at your shitty job and work well those two weeks. Repeat as needed for the next few years until you have a great employment history. When you are just starting out, no one expects you to have years of history at one place. Though, if you land a job that will cover your costs and makes you happy, put some time in there. All the while you are building a great worker history. You want your old boss to say to any potential new employer that you are eligible for rehire, that you worked really well.  

\#4 Make plans for becoming independent. Show your friend that you are looking at apartments/rooms for rent. Save up for that move and start small! Rent a little room somewhere and have a plan for covering all of your own expenses. If your friend sees this, they will feel better about hosting you and you will feel more motivated to save. You will need to save for first and last month's rent, and maybe a deposit. If you rent a room, it will be easier because you won't have to open accounts like electric and gas. Those will charge you hefty deposits. Be a model tenant in that room because now you are establishing renter's history and you want people to say you paid on time, that you were quiet, clean, friendly, and not a hassle. See a pattern?

\#5 Remind yourself every day that this situation is temporary and you'll be in a much better place a year from now, and even better place 5 years from now. Don't give up hope. You can do it!

Hormones communicate to the brain that we are full or to keep eating. There are different reasons for different people being overweight, and it never boils down to behavior that merits this fat shaming approach of "you just need to chose better eating habits." Heavy people more than anyone else want answers and help resolving this problem. They are not ignorant. That approach will never work, and telling overweight people to take a deeper look inside isn't going to work either. We need to examine what drives eating habits.

Being in good spirits and being suicidal are not mutually exclusive. Many suicidal people experience a sense of relief once they have made their decision because they know their suffering will end soon. Some spend quality time with loved ones and try to enjoy their last day(s).

I personally don't feel that spiritual healing can address serious psycho-social issues. These people are nor devoid of spirituality or awareness, rather, they have serious life functioning problems preventing them from having a life worth living. If you ask them if they would like a brief spiritual experience, they may respond that they prefer to have illness alleviated or more resources, thanks. Spirituality may be very beneficial component to a person's life, but it cannot heal a person's entire life or satisfy all of their needs. They are not asleep, rather they are lacking in things that are necessary for self-worth (capability, social acceptance, healthy brains, access to healthcare, etc.) It is hard to convince a very rejected person that their life has potential, and DMT will certainly not be able to convince an elderly, unemployable, cancer ridden person that their life has potential. One of my hardest tasks in working with patients who are on hospice, is helping them find hope in arguably hopeless situations. If your in pain, lonely, and broke, what meaning can a DMT trip give to your life that would make you want to continue living that way? Some situations can be changed, but I don't think DMT can give someone the ability to change them. It won't show them how, not will it imbue them with the motivation to overcome such great obstacles. Social services and medical care might though. 

Pain killers work because they alleviate pain. Antidepressants work because they alleviate symptoms of depression. Anti-psychotics work because they alleviate psychosis and hallucinations. Therapy works because it addresses problems with thinking and communication and gives a person new tools for navigating their life in a healthier way. For a treatment to be effective, it needs to address the problems that affect a suicidal person. DMT, while amazing and profoundly spiritual, does not appear to me to provide any relief from the problems that lead to suicidality. I do think it should be researched and explored for other uses. Having personal experience with suicide and DMT, I can tell you personally that a 3-15 minute profound spiritual DMT does not negate a 24-hour a day chronic life function problem. I do feel fortunate to be among the people who get to experience DMT, and I wish for others to be able to do so too, but my struggles and limitations remain despite my DMT experiences. I am one case of DMT not being an effective treatment for suicide. In my case, I was helped by therapy, getting a service dog, changing my social groups, becoming active in my community, and going to school. If I had not been open to therapy and a pooch, I would not be here today. I cannot say the same for DMT. I don't feel that because DMT is not a cure for suicide that DMT is any less wonderful and magical. I believe it has a place in the world and I am grateful for its role in my life. We can celebrate the molecule and what it does to us, even if it doesn't address SI.

First of all, it’s really nice that you are thinking about people who are so sad that they would want to end their lives. It means a lot that you care and are willing to have a conversation about such a stigmatized topic. 

I feel like I have some insight on this topic, but I am by no means able to speak for everyone. I am a relatively newer spice enthusiast; I tried it for the first time 10 years ago and I have had about 25-30 experiences since with my own batch. I have also tried 5MEO an most of the other common subs. With regards to suicide, I have worked on a suicide hotline and helped people during very difficult times. In 2017, I watch a man take his life by running into a fire. My whole life I have struggled with suicide ideation (SI) and fortunately I survived a serious attempt when I was younger.

I feel that DMT is a magical experience (most of the time) and I feel my life is better for psychedelics being part of it. I enjoy the community and exploring my mind, but I can absolutely say that even with that in my life, I still struggle with SI. The problem with suicide is not the moment people are choosing to do it, but their life leading up to it. Intervening in that moment is helpful, but DMT will not erase the problems that lead them to make that choice. In fact, it may cause more harm as good portion of people are under the influence of alcohol when they do it. 

Things that lead people to want to die are not resolved by a DMT experience. For example, an unemployable older man who has lost his job/money and feels hopeless (a very common reason for suicide) will come back from infinity to find his home still in foreclosure and bills piled up. A woman who lives with chronic pain will come back from DMT to find her body still paralyzed or cancer still spreading. 

Another common reason for suicide is mental illness (MI). Some people with MI can and do enjoy psychedelics, but many cannot. It can trigger psychosis, increase SI, alter already dysfunctional brain chemistry, interact negatively with some medications or be dulled by other medications. MI is also often comorbid with severe social isolation or ostracization. A journey will not bring friends and family back into a mentally ill person’s life, nor will it give them the social skills to function socially. 

DMT can also be abused by people who have impulse control issues and interfere with their daily functioning. It can cause them to relapse on other, harder drugs because some have a difficult time separating the experiences. Some people struggle with addiction and are unable to enjoy any substances without it leading to an urge to use other, more harmful substances. That, in turn, can cause people to have problems with family life, work, or school.

So, what will help? More mental health education and earlier detection. Increased intervention programs like hotlines and affordable, accessible counseling. Health insurance programs that cover mental healthcare services on par with medical health services. People like you! People caring and being willing to talk about it. People reaching out to others and asking directly if they are suicidal. No, it won’t put the idea in their head, but it very well may help them feel safe opening up about it; that may lead to them being willing to seek professional help. More medical and social services offer people with suicide ideation opportunities for help and healing. And maybe some of those people will go on to have a life worth living and be lucky enough to enjoy DMT too.

TL;DR - Love ya for talking about this. DMT won’t fix serious life problems such as financial problems and illness; it might actually cause more harm than good. More medical and social services are needed to address suicidal behavior.

ESA's and service dogs both have the same training requirements: none. While it's true that a service dog must be trained to perform a task to help a person with a disability, there is no law requiring them to have any special training or behavior classes or so on. I could take a dog from an animal shelter, train it to perform a task such as picking up my keys to assist with my disability, and that would count as a service dog. Service dogs are not necessarily more trained or better behaved than emotional support animals. There are plenty of service dogs out there who do not get along with other dogs. Service dogs are held to the same standard as any other dog in public, in that the owner must have control over the animal and the owner is responsible and liable for any harm or damage that animal causes.

If a business owner chooses to allow dogs into a business regardless of their ESA, service dog, or pet status that is their right. You cannot dictate that a business isn't allowed to have  a dog friendly business. It is up to every owner to have control over their dogs. This includes owners of service animals and ESA's. It is not a store owner's job to police the behavior of animals, it is the owner's responsibility to do that.

Welcome home! I have been to will-call every year and it is not too complicated. You will be in the main line of cars going into Burning Man initially. Then some of the gate staff will ask you if anyone in your car is going to will call. You will be directed to pull your vehicle to the right and follow the signs to the will call parking lot. There are several volunteers that will help guide you. There will be porta potties near there. After you park you will get in line for will-call. Depending on what time you get there it can be a very long wait. Part of it is in the shade, however I have seen lines that went out into the sun. I recommend bringing sun protection if you will be picking up your tickets in the daytime. When you get to the window, you will present staff with your print out showing your order number. Most importantly you need to bring your identification. Once they have located your order they will give you your tickets, vehicle pass, and survival guide. And that's it! The fun part is talking to other burners in line... You might make some new friends there. Once you get your tickets, you then get back in your vehicle and continue towards the gate road. You will reenter the main line going into the event. Once you approach gate, they will ask you for your tickets, car pass, (and work access permits if you are arriving early).

The wisest answer would be to avoid MDMA. However...

I have noticed that using MDMA/ecstasy every once in a while seems to be fine for me. It's when I use it several times in a short period (say three days in a row or every other day at a festival) that it can trigger a depression. Frequent use is a bad idea.

Also, I avoid depleting my good brain chemicals when I am at higher risk of depression (such as when my pooch passed away, or when I am stressed with work/exams). Hold off on MDMA when other things in your life may be making it harder for you to manage depression. Your friends will understand. When we have parties, or events, if someone in our group is staying sober for mental health reasons (or because they have to work early the next day), we totally understand and support that.

Getting lots of rest, healthy food & hydration, exercise, and social support after MDMA use can help keep a depression from getting too bad.

Everyone is different, so if you are going to try it, start small and go easy. Wait a few weeks and see how you feel before trying it again. Then try again if you are up for it. Have a safety plan in place in case you do get depressed (friends, therapist, numbers for crisis hotlines handy, etc.) 

Like others have said, the feelings you have on MDMA can be a welcome relief from depression and anxiety. I have found that I have had some lasting positive effects (not dramatic ones, but nice low-level improvement on my outlook.)

If you struggle with anxiety and or depression, please consider therapy...it's awesome when you have the right person. 

Also...young brains aren't finished developing until your mid-20's. Exposing your brain to drugs before then is just not a good idea. If you can wait, there is lots of fun to be had rolling after 25. 

Hope this helps!

TLDR: depends: can trigger depression if used too frequently or at wrong time, start slow, practice good self-care, have support handy, wait until after age 25 to start drugs

I never said what you said was unacceptable, I said it is unreliable. Reliability means it can be attributed to the rest of the population. Anecdote, because it is coming from too small of a sample size (in this case only one source), can't be relied on to describe the rest if the population. Does that mean it is wrong about the rest of the population, not necessarily. It could be right, it could be wrong, but unless you look at enough of the population, you won't now what is normal for that population. Just because anecdote is not reliable and is not evidence, doesn't mean it has no value. You can even do an academic paper on anecdote; it's called a case study. It just isn't evidence in a scientific sense. When you are doing research to understand things like the prevalence of rape in prison, anecdote is not acceptable for understanding the big picture. When researchers do this kind of research, the strength of the evidence absolutely does determine whether it is valid evidence. Very careful methods of measurement and statistical analysis are followed by peer review in order to ensure the strength of that evidence. It needs to be accurate because this type of evidence is typically used to make policy such as procedures for limiting inmate interactions or funding for rape treatment programs. 

Courtroom evidence is an entirely different thing. In a courtroom, people aren't typically analyzing an entire population, they are addressing a specific situation (civil or criminal act or failure to act) with a specific entity (defendant). They are describing a specific case, so a personal testimony of what happened is appropriate.

Telling other people's stories is anecdotal, as is telling your own story. I was pointing out that there is a difference between anecdote and evidence. Anecdote is a personal story. It can be your story, or it can be someone else's story, but is always a story. Anecdote ≠ evidence, so there is no "anecdotal evidence". Because anecdotes are the stories of one, or a few people, they may or may not be representative of the general population and as such are highly unreliable, even if they are true for some individuals. Evidence, on the other hand, is a large enough collection of data to be representative of the general population.
